back: A micro-organism (fungus, bacterium or virus) that causes plant disease.
An organism, usually an insect, that carries a pathogen from diseased to healthy plants (leafhoppers carry maize streak virus).
Fungal: spots, rings, rusts, powdery growth, rots. Bacterial: water-soaked spots, sudden wilt, soft rots, ooze. Viral: mosaic, streaks, curl, stunting.
Wind, water splash and irrigation, insect vectors, seed and planting material, soil and residues, tools and hands.
Fungal; rectangular grey lesions between veins; favoured by humid weather and maize residue; rotation, resistant varieties, fungicide.
Soil-borne bacterium of tomato, potato and relatives; sudden wilt of green plants, ooze from cut stem; no chemical cure: rotation, clean seedlings, hygiene.
Mosaic and distorted leaves; spread on hands, tools and from tobacco products; wash hands, remove plants, resistant varieties.
Protectant: surface layer, before infection, renew after rain (copper, sulfur). Systemic: absorbed, can stop early infections.
